clue.text: New leader of the Blues backed in home ground

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters before it are pulverised and remixed

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly chosen party chief returns to their home turf with backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' and 'home ground' read as support on familiar territory, but all three words are just fodder. Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, whose leader since 2024 is Kemi Badenoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Kemi Badenoch became Conservative Party leader in November 2024, and Tories are nicknamed the Blues after their party colour.

clue.text: Revered figure needing a shrink to get sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out means putting into a different order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; a shrink is slang for a psychiatrist in the surface

explanation.surface: Some venerated person is so troubled they need therapy to get their head straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' plays on therapy fixing someone, but here it scrambles the letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Krishna is a major Hindu deity, worshipped as an avatar of Vishnu, so certainly a revered figure.

clue.text: Flipping unhappy setter's someone punished for greed

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the words that follow are read backwards

blocks.note: a direct synonym
the setter refers to themself, so setter's is 'I am', shortened

explanation.surface: A furious, miserable crossword compiler has been penalised for being greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive meaning 'damned', but it is the signal to read the phrase backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth King Midas wished that all he touched would turn to gold, and was cursed when even his food did.

clue.text: Dancer from Ireland entering dance area

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the word for the country sits within the words that follow

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A performer from Ireland walks onto the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, so she is a particular kind of dancer.

clue.text: Owing pounds leads to fight between gentlemen

blocks.note: money that is due is owed
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: An unpaid debt provokes two gentlemen to come to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' looks like a placement instruction but simply joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel was a formal combat between two gentlemen settling a point of honour with pistols or swords.

clue.text: Observing what an undecorated cake has? About time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase goes around the letter for the final word

blocks.note: a plain cake has no icing on it
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Watching a bare, un-iced cake, someone exclaims impatiently that it's high time it was finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exasperated exclamation, but splits into a container signal and the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to observe or become aware of something, so noticing and observing are synonyms.

clue.text: Transport for Bedouin maybe turned up on line

blocks.note: someone who turned up came along
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A desert nomad's ride was flipped over while on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' tempts a reversal, but it simply means arrived; 'on' places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are the traditional pack and riding animals of the Bedouin desert nomads; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Reprimand an attractive person around the start of the week

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first phrase is wrapped about the abbreviation for the weekday

blocks.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person; an gives A
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a good-looking colleague at the beginning of the working week.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to warn or rebuke someone firmly, the same as reprimanding them.

clue.text: Puzzle with hot drink and occasional servings of sherry

indicators.note: occasional means only now and then, so just every other letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: tea is a hot drink
the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A brain-teaser enjoyed with a cup of tea and the odd glass of sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser, short for brain-teaser, is a puzzling problem or riddle.

clue.text: Tolerant of popular and mostly boring chap

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: something in is fashionable or popular
a direct synonym
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone is fairly lenient towards a well-liked but rather tedious man.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indulgent means readily allowing others' wishes or faults, which is what being tolerant involves.

clue.text: Fly east on fighter plane carrying diamonds

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the aircraft name encloses the card-suit letter

blocks.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
D abbreviates the card suit diamonds
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A jet heads eastwards with a cargo of gems on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about piloting, but it is the noun being defined. 'On' places the east letter after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged insect, a type of fly that bites in swarms.

clue.text: Husband, you heard, cast off and told to be quiet

indicators.note: heard signals the letter that sounds like the word you when spoken

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
the letter U is pronounced like the word
to shed is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A husband is abandoned by his wife and ordered to keep his mouth shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hushed has been silenced or shushed, so they have been made quiet on instruction.

clue.text: Little Sally eating cold cuts and shellfish

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the short name swallows the letter for cold

blocks.note: Sal is a pet form of the name Sally
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A young girl is tucking into sliced cold meats and seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold cuts' reads as one phrase for sliced meat, but it splits: cold is a letter inside the name, cuts is a separate verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are bivalve molluscs with fan-shaped shells, a well-known kind of shellfish.

clue.text: BBC One plugging a tune that's broadcast

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so the numeral letter sits inside the rearranged phrase
broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The BBC's main channel is promoting a song it has put on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'BBC One' reads as the TV channel, but the two words split: BBC is the definition and One is the numeral. Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, is a long-standing affectionate nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's public broadcaster has been nicknamed Auntie for its supposedly prim, motherly tone.

clue.text: Yearn to enter Reno, travelling around? Not any more

indicators.note: travelling around means moving all over, so the city's letters are shifted into a new order
to enter means to go inside, so the word for yearn is placed within the rearranged city

blocks.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
the Nevada city, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone longing to visit Reno while touring ends up saying they will not do it again.
explanation.definitionFit: No longer is an idiom meaning formerly but not now, the same sense as not any more.

clue.text: Deduce touring Brazilian city is second-rate

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the verb wraps itself around the city name

blocks.note: to infer is to deduce
Rio de Janeiro, usually just Rio

explanation.surface: A traveller concludes that a trip around a Brazilian city is disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inferior is of lower quality, which is what second-rate describes.

clue.text: Using some sweetener, get ice-cream very zesty

indicators.note: using only some of the words means the letters lie inside the run of text that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Adding sugar substitute to ice cream makes it really tangy.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest means vigour and enthusiasm, so someone very zesty is lively and full of energy.

clue.text: A little unwell, as an eagle is?

blocks.note: first meaning: feeling slightly off-colour
second meaning: in golf, a hole completed in fewer strokes than standard

explanation.walkthrough: The eagle looks like the bird, but in golf an eagle is a score two strokes under the standard for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means not quite well, and an eagle in golf is literally two strokes beneath the expected score.

clue.text: Someone who plunders beer — roughly 3.14 litres to start with

indicators.note: to start with means placed at the beginning, so the number and unit come ahead of the drink

blocks.note: pi is approximately 3.14
L is the abbreviation for litres
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A looter drinks beer, starting with just over three litres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' puts the number and the unit before the drink. 'Roughly 3.14' looks like a measured quantity of beer, but it is the value of pi.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillage is to plunder or loot, so one who pillages is a plunderer.

clue.text: Slavic language shows refinement

blocks.note: first meaning: the language of Poland
second meaning: elegance or sophistication of manner

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are pronounced differently, which hides the link between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is the West Slavic tongue of Poland, and polish also means cultivated elegance or finish.

clue.text: Dance music number after covers from The Clash

indicators.note: covers are the outside layers, so only the first and last letters of each word are used
after means coming later, so the abbreviation for number goes at the end

blocks.note: the outside letters of each of the two words
No is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A band plays cover versions of The Clash's songs in a club music style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like cover versions by a band, given The Clash are a punk group, but it means the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Techno is a style of electronic dance music with a fast, repetitive beat that began in 1980s Detroit.

clue.text: Remain longer than son in exposed Scottish river

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for son inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: something out is in the open, exposed
S is the abbreviation for son
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A boy stays too long, standing unprotected in a river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay someone is to stay beyond the time they do, as in outstaying one's welcome.

clue.text: Arthurian knight has jousting equipment, given large quantity

blocks.note: a lance is the long spear used in jousting
a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: A knight of King Arthur's court is supplied with plenty of jousting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous of King Arthur's Knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Devour ends of aubergine moussaka that you keep

indicators.note: ends are the final letters, so the last letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of each of these five words

explanation.walkthrough: The indicator seems to cover only the first two words, but it reaches all five words to the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat up is a phrasal verb meaning to consume all of something, a synonym for devouring it.

clue.text: A bit of photomontage is thrilling for discriminating type

indicators.note: a bit of means only a part, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.walkthrough: 'Discriminating' suggests a connoisseur with refined taste, but here it means prejudiced.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist is someone who treats people unfairly because of their age, a person prejudiced against a group.

clue.text: Current business agreement for wonderful model

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
a deal is a business arrangement

explanation.surface: A topical commercial contract suits a top fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or standard to aspire to, which is a model of excellence.

clue.text: Little daughter, one not welcome in the garden?

definitions.text: one not welcome in the garden

blocks.note: wee is Scottish and informal British for small
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A small girl is being kept out of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is any plant growing where a gardener does not want it, an unwanted intruder in the beds.

clue.text: In America, little money on the radio for track

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the answer sounds like the coin's name

blocks.note: a cent is a small US coin, one hundredth of a dollar

clue.text: Arrangement of pet sitter fairer than all the others

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal-minder's booking system is more even-handed than any rival's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairer' suggests more just, but here it means more beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old word for beautiful, so fairest of all means the most attractive, the superlative of pretty.

clue.text: Playing Coldplay airs every now and again

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters are moved around freely

blocks.note: taken as written; Coldplay is a British rock band
